title: Hiring Sprint OPERA Playbook — 30/60/90 Impact
summary: A compact, operational playbook to move from sourcing to first-90-day impact for IC and manager hires. Focused on a 30/60/90 activation sprint (OPERA = Onboard, Probe, Enable, Ramp, Assess) to align hiring partners, interviewers, and onboarding owners around observable signals of success.
background: People Ops frequently runs ad-hoc handoffs between recruiting, hiring managers, and onboarding. This doc defines a repeatable sprint (OPERA) to shorten time-to-impact and make interview decisions more predictive of first-quarter outcomes. It intentionally blends hiring plan cadence, a behavioral+skills rubric, and a prioritized onboarding checklist with explicit owners.
hiring_plan: Goal: hire 3 mid-senior backend engineers and 1 product manager in Q3 for infra and product platform teams. Timebox: 6-week active sourcing window per role (sourcing -> onsites -> offer). Buffer: 2-week overlap with new-hire prep before start date. Key constraints: interview panel availability, compensation calibration, relocation window. Commitments: recruiting to present 6 qualified pipelined candidates per role by week 3; hiring manager to complete final calibration with People Ops by end of week 2.
roles_and_headcount: Open roles: infra-backend-engineer (3), platform-product-manager (1). Leveling guidance: IC3-IC4 for backend (expect distributed systems experience, benchmarks: latency reduction feature ownership, 1 shipped service), PM3 for product (experience owning infra-facing features). Hiring manager must attach role one-pager with success metrics and top-3 deliverables for first 90 days to job req.
success_metrics: Primary: time-to-first-meaningful-PR/feature (target 30 days for backend), number of completed onboarding demos and peer reviews (target 3 demos by day 60), retention risk signal (engagement score <60 by day 30 triggers manager intervention). Hiring funnel metrics: offer-to-accept ratio (target >= 0.6), interview-to-offer pass rate (target 12-15%).
interview_rubric: High-level rubric (behavioral + skills). Scoring: 1-4 (1 = no evidence, 4 = exceptional). Dimensions: technical-scope (architecture & system design), implementation-craft (coding, tests, debugging), product-sense (for PM role), collaboration & feedback (peer communication, code review), ownership & outcomes (drives to measurable results), role-fit & signals (motivation, team chemistry). Interviewers explicitly note examples mapped to rubric behaviors (e.g., 'designed async retry strategy to reduce tail latency' -> technical-scope score 3). Reject reason taxonomy: competence-gap, scope-mismatch, culture-misfit, compensation-misalignment.
interview_process_flow: Week 0: hiring brief + scorecard attached to req. Week 1-3: phone screen (recruiter), technical screen (engineer), take-home or whiteboard exercise (if applicable). Week 4: onsite loop (3-4 interviews + hiring manager), hiring debrief within 48 hours. People Ops coordinates compensation band check and reference check. Offer sent within 3 business days post-debrief. If candidate passes but final committee requests more evidence, schedule a focused follow-up (max 7 days).
score_template: Each interviewer fills scorecard with: role, date, rubric scores (six dimensions), top-2 strengths, top-2 risks, recommended-next-step (reject, hire, hold-needs-followup), confidence-level (low/medium/high). Composite decision: majority hire and average score >= 3.2, OR hiring manager + one lead approve with documented mitigation plan for specific risks.
onboarding_checklist: Pre-day0: create account and invite to Slack + email; confirm hardware order and VPN access
Pre-day0: manager fills 90-day impact sheet and schedules week1/2/4 syncs
Day0-1: welcome call with People Ops (benefits, payroll, logistics); 30-min team welcome + 60-min product/tech overview
Week1: environment setup (repo access, dev creds), run local build, smoke test deployment - success signoff by buddy
Week1-2: shadow sessions — 2 code reviews, 1 onboarding pairing task; buddy to run daily 30-min check-ins
Week3-4: first small feature/bug with code owner review and delivery (target PR merged)
Week5-8: independent work on scoped ticket, present technical demo to team by day 60
Day30, Day60, Day90: structured manager check-ins using OPERA assessment template; collect self-eval + peer feedback
By Day90: final review — evidence of impact (metrics, merged work, demos), plan for next 90 days with stretch goals
escalation_rules: If any of the following occurs, trigger People Ops touchpoint within 48 hours: onboarding blocker preventing dev environment setup beyond day 3, candidate declines offer after verbal acceptance, manager confidence-level 'low' at day 30. For retention risk indicated in pulse <60, schedule calibration with engineering lead and People Ops within 5 business days.
retrospective_and_iteration: After each hiring sprint, convene a 60-min retro with recruiting, hiring manager, key interviewers, and People Ops. Capture 3 wins, 3 pain points, and 3 experiments for next sprint. Feed experiment list into hiring-process backlog (Linear) and tag by priority. Retro note template: date, roles hired, time-to-offer, quality-signal (first-90-day pass/fail), actions.
notes: This playbook is intentionally condensed for fast adoption. Localize for international hires (visa timeline, relocation, and tax). Use OPERA shorthand in calendar invites to keep alignment language consistent. Expect minor tweaks to rubric thresholds by team after two sprints.
next_steps: 1) Run a pilot for infra-backend-engineer role starting 2025-07-07. 2) Share playbook with hiring managers and recruiting by 2025-07-03. 3) Schedule retro 4 weeks after first hire start date.
